All are architects of Fate,
Working in these walls of Time;
Some with massive deeds and great,
Some with ornaments of rhyme.

Nothing useless is, or low;
Each thing in its place is best;
And what seems but idle show
Strengthens and supports the rest.

For the structure that we raise,
Time is with materials filled;
Our to-days and yesterdays
Are the blocks with which we build.

Truly shape and fashion these;
Leave no yawning gaps between;
Think not, because no man sees,
Such things will remain unseen.

In the elder days of Art,
Builders wrought with greatest care
Each minute and unseen part;
For the Gods see everywhere.

Let us do our work as well,
Both the unseen and the seen;
Make the house, where Gods may dwell,
Beautiful, entire, and clean.

Else our lives are incomplete,
Standing in these walls of Time,
Broken stairways, where the feet
Stumble as they seek to climb.

Build to-day, then, strong and sure,
With a firm and ample base;
And ascending and secure
Shall to-morrow find its place.

Thus alone can we attain
To those turrets, where the eye
Sees the world as one vast plain,
And one boundless reach of sky.

I was 22yo and home alone a few days after getting a tonsillectomy. The cauterization in my throat popped and I started spewing blood out of my mouth. I grabbed a 12oz plastic keg cup to hold over my mouth while I drove myself a couple miles to the hospital. I filled the plastic cup with my blood to the brim 3x by the time I made it to the hospital. Squealing tire into the horse-shoe parking area in front of the hospital I was rushing toward the front doors, when I heard some bitch say in a snobby tone, "Oh, he must be in a hurry." I chucked my full cup of blood a couple of feet away from her feet on the sidewalk and she let out the best hair curling scream I've heard in my life (in retrospect I feel terrible for who ever had to clean that up). I made it to the hospital and was checked in over night. The following morning it happened again..... The clots in my throat opened up again and I had to go through the whole process again. While they rushed me to the ER the blood leaking in my throat was making it hard to breath. I could hear young nurses panicking in the background, which made me even more nervous. The feeling in my finger tips and toes starts to go cold & numb, my vision started to become a saturated & grayscaled, and right when I thought "this might be it" they gassed me and shot me up with anesthesia. Needless to say I was relieved to wake-up after the 2nd surgery. I did make a full recovery.

TL;DR: Have tonsils removed and go home, home alone and bleeding out of my mouth I drive myself to hospital and stay the night, start bleeding out of my mouth again the following morning, get rushed into ER for follow-up surgery, survive.
